use_snapshot <- FALSE

# Data

This chunk is complete. It fetches all BRAF and TP53 mutations in the TCGA
melanoma study from the cBioPortal API and keeps one row per mutation.

```{r fetch}
study <- "skcm_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018"
genes <- c(BRAF = 673, TP53 = 7157)   # cBioPortal uses Entrez gene IDs

fetch_gene <- function(gene) {
  api_url <- paste0(
    "https://www.cbioportal.org/api/molecular-profiles/", study, "_mutations/mutations",
    "?sampleListId=", study, "_sequenced",
    "&entrezGeneId=", genes[[gene]], "&projection=SUMMARY&pageSize=10000")
  x <- fromJSON(api_url)
  data.frame(gene = gene, sample_id = x$sampleId, patient_id = x$patientId,
             protein_change = x$proteinChange, protein_start = x$proteinPosStart,
             mutation_type = x$mutationType)
}

read_snapshot <- function() {
  file <- "data/skcm-mutations-2026-11-18.csv"
  if (!file.exists(file)) file <- paste0(
    "https://henriksson-lab.github.io/course_cellbiology/bioinfo-cancer-genomics/", file)
  read.csv(file)
}

mutations <- NULL
if (!use_snapshot) {
  mutations <- tryCatch(do.call(rbind, lapply(names(genes), fetch_gene)),
                        error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(mutations)) retrieved <- as.character(Sys.Date())
}
if (is.null(mutations)) mutations <- read_snapshot()

table(mutations$gene)
```

Source: `r data_source`, study `r study`; retrieved `r retrieved`.

# 1. Where are the mutations?

Fill in the blank: put the amino-acid position on the x axis.

```{r lollipop, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
mapped <- subset(mutations, !is.na(protein_start))
per_position <- aggregate(sample_id ~ gene + protein_start, data = mapped, FUN = length)
names(per_position)[3] <- "records"

ggplot(per_position, aes(x = ___, y = records)) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = protein_start, y = 0, yend = records), colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(colour = "#a8324a") +
  facet_wrap(~ gene, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Amino-acid position", y = "Mutations at this position",
       caption = paste0("Data: cBioPortal, TCGA melanoma; retrieved ", retrieved))
```
